newsitem.title: USA: Avalanches in Utah kill one, injure two.
newsitem.headline: Avalanches in Utah kill one, injure two.

text.p: Heavy snows coupled with high winds caused four avalanches in the mountains in the past four days, leaving one person dead and injuring two, officials said on Sunday.
Doug Hall, 27, of Silverton, Colorado, was ice climbing on Saturday in the Bridal Veil Falls area of Provo Canyon when an avalanche swept him nearly 250 feet (75 metres) down a canyon wall.
Attempts by a Utah County Search and Rescue Team to revive Hall after he was found were futile, said Utah County sheriff's spokesman Lt. Ron Fernstedt.
Hall's climbing partner, Scott Lee, 25, of Sandy, Utah, suffered head, back and chest injuries in the slide. He was listed in satisfactory condition on Sunday morning, a hospital spokeswoman said.
Three other ice climbers were partially buried in the slide, but were unharmed, Fernstedt said.

A 22-year-old Sandy, Utah woman and her friend were in the Butler Fork area of Big Cottonwood Canyon in Salt Lake County on Saturday when a large snow slide swept her 20 feet (six metres) down a slope, leaving her buried for nearly 90 minutes.

Camille Coyle survived by creating a five-inch (13 cms) air space for herself by moving her head back and forth as soon as she realised she was buried, said Salt Lake County sheriff's deputy Dave Nelson.
"It was amazing she survived for an hour and a half. I don't often call things miraculous, but there is no other word for it," Nelson said.
